name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.169.0 — A mock-page note can now mark an area: drag a rectangle over any part of a served mock and the note lands on that content at every viewport width, painted in its status colour by the notes layer. The box is stored as a fraction of the smallest element containing it with the covered children as the reflow fallback, so it re-finds its spot or honestly reports itself outdated and offers re-placement. The owner's card beside the box carries accept, reject with a reason, resolve, withdraw and delete behind an undoable toast. 7.168.0 — Test expiry deletions land in their own commit after the close commit, so the close commit stays the tree the review judged and replay's coverage leg no longer starts from a tree missing the coverage it just passed. 7.167.0 — replay --select now skips any candidate review run already named by a pristine-red setup-failed replay row — a standing claim that the target's tree cannot be rebuilt into the state its CLEAN review judged (a close-time expiry sweep deleting a test the review's own coverage leg counted is the recorded cause). Such rows record no measurement and so never advance the dueness window; without the skip the same unreproducible target was re-picked on every run, burning a full setup cycle each time and leaving the harness due forever. When every candidate in the window is so claimed, --select refuses with its own named exit-1 message rather than the generic no-eligible-row one.
